events.name: valence_salience_listener
events.hypothesis: Listeners interpret evaluative descriptions (such as a speaker referring to their favorite or least favorite object) by modulating their referent prior with the valence of the framing. Positive valence increases the prior expectation of feature-rich referents, whereas negative valence inverts this preference to favor minimal or feature-sparse referents. This evaluative prior is shared as common ground across the simulated literal listener and the pragmatic listener.

events.name: naive_speaker_listener
events.hypothesis: People interpret referential descriptions by inverting a naive generative speaker who mentions any true feature of the intended object with equal probability, rather than simulating a speaker who mentalizes a listener. When hearing an ambiguous word, listeners favor objects with fewer total features because a naive speaker is less likely to have chosen that word for an object with many competing features. On displays where a multi-featured object has only uninformative alternative features, this model predicts listeners will disfavor it relative to an object with fewer features, whereas standard RSA predicts listeners will favor it because a strategic speaker avoids uninformative alternatives.

events.name: costly_feature_speaker
events.hypothesis: Speakers trade off communicative informativeness with utterance costs that favor accessible, shared descriptors over narrow, highly specific words. Pragmatic listeners invert this speaker, recognizing that a speaker who uses a shared word may still refer to an object with unique features because specific words carry higher production costs.

events.name: rsa_l2_shared_prior
events.hypothesis:
Listeners reason at depth 2 by inverting a speaker who anticipates the depth-1 pragmatic listener, maintaining the common-knowledge salience prior (feature count and familiarization base rate) across all levels of recursion. Reasoning two levels deep allows the speaker to select utterances based on pragmatic implicatures rather than just literal comprehension, resolving ambiguous references in complex displays where depth-1 reasoning under-discriminates.

- Recursion depth: choice_probs calls L2 instead of L1.

- Parameters added or removed: None (retains alpha, w_features, w_familiar, lapse with identical priors).

Pragmatic listeners invert a speaker who communicates with these graded semantic representations, sharpening preference for minimal, prototypical exemplars.

Incorporating a decision rationality parameter for the listener into the depth-2 evaluative architecture better captures the high determinism of participant choices on clear communicative displays.
